title: Lift yourself by yourself (6.1–6.9)
hook: the verse that says you are your own best friend, and your own worst enemy

segments.voice: Yesterday, the end of chapter five: the sage's peace, from the friend of all beings. Your line was peace. Today, chapter six, the chapter of meditation, and a friend much closer to home. Day one hundred seventy-eight.

Listen to the voice in your head for a minute after something goes wrong. You dropped the ball at work. You snapped at someone you love. What does the voice say? For a lot of people it says things they would never say to a friend. You always do this. What's wrong with you. If a stranger talked to you like that, you'd walk away. But this voice comes along everywhere. Chapter six of the Gita opens with two lines that millions of people know by heart, and they're about exactly this voice.
screen: `SOMETHING GOES WRONG.` → `WHAT DOES THE VOICE SAY?` → `WORDS YOU'D NEVER SAY TO A FRIEND.`

segments.voice: First, Krishna clears something up. The true renouncer, verse one says, isn't the one who stops lighting the sacred fire or stops doing any work. It's the one who does what needs doing without leaning on the fruit. Then verse three: for someone climbing toward yoga, action is the way up. For someone who has arrived, stillness is the way. And then verses five and six. Lift yourself by yourself; don't let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self. In Sanskrit the same word, atman, the self, comes again and again, like a mirror facing a mirror. The word for friend is bandhu: a friend, and also family, the one bound to you. Verse six explains how the same self can be both. For the one who has mastered themselves, the self is a friend. For the one who hasn't, the self behaves like an enemy. Notice what the verse doesn't say. It doesn't say wait for someone to rescue you. It doesn't say you're on your own, either; the Gita is full of grace. It says the hand that lifts you starts with your own. The chapter then paints the one who has done it: steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, praise and blame. A lump of earth, a stone and gold look alike to them. And they're even-minded toward friend and foe, the good and the bad. That's today's word. Lift yourself by yourself. Be your own friend.
screen: `THE TRUE RENOUNCER STILL ACTS.` · `LIFT YOURSELF BY YOURSELF.` · `THE SELF: FRIEND OR ENEMY.` · `EARTH, STONE AND GOLD ALIKE.` · then, large: `BE YOUR OWN FRIEND.`

segments.voice: Sit, and think of the last time the inner voice was harsh with you. Let the words come up. Now imagine a good friend heard those words said about you. What would the friend say back? Let that answer come up, in a warm voice. Breathe with it. On each in-breath, lift, just a little, the way you'd lift someone off the floor. On each out-breath, let yourself be held. The bell holds the time.
Lift yourself by yourself. Gita six, five: the self is the friend of the self, and the enemy of the self. The lifting starts with your own hand.
Your line: your own friend. Today, once, catch the harsh voice, and answer it the way a friend would. Day one hundred seventy-eight.

howItsDone: Gita 6.5 is one of the most memorized verses of the Gita; many Hindus learn it by heart and recite it as encouragement in hard times.

fork.setup: you're sinking. the Gita says the lift starts where?
options: with yourself: lift yourself by yourself.
fork.reveal: with yourself. verse 5: lift yourself by yourself, don't let yourself sink; the self is its own friend.

original.note: Sanskrit: bandhu, friend or kin; from a root meaning to bind. the self is its own bandhu (6.5).

trapdoor: what you thought: pull yourself up by your bootstraps.
what it means: the self can be friend or enemy to itself; the lifting begins with your own hand, and with kindness.
what a scholar hears: 6.5, uddhared atmanatmanam, repeats atman in several cases in a single line; bandhu comes from bandh, to bind, so the friend is the one bound to you.

notes: 'Millions of people know it by heart' is a general claim about 6.5's popularity; soften if needed.
The inner-critic framing is a modern application; the verse's 'self' (atman) is read differently by schools (lower self lifted by higher self, mind by mind). Consider a note on that in a later level.
